headline: Dubai Environment Conference opens with focus on air, water and waste management
deck: DECCA convenes the inaugural DECE at Grand Hyatt Dubai on 7 September with six focus areas spanning biodiversity, climate change and circular economy.
excerpt: The Dubai Environment Conference & Exhibition opens on 7 September as the government's flagship sustainability event. It brings together environmental regulators, sustainability officers and climate specialists to align regional strategies on emissions reduction, water quality and waste recycling.
content:
The Dubai Environment Conference & Exhibition opens at the Grand Hyatt on 7 September, organised by the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum. The inaugural conference brings together government officials, corporate decision-makers, environmental specialists and researchers across six focus areas: biodiversity, natural resources, food security, climate change, circular economy and environmental artificial intelligence.

The conference marks a shift in Dubai's sustainability focus from isolated project-based initiatives to a holistic framework aligned with the UAE's Net Zero 2050 commitment. The emirate has committed to Net Zero by 2050, and the conference delivers measurable progress targets for 2026-2030. Biodiversity protection encompasses habitat restoration in coastal and desert zones, following the UAE's commitments under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework signed at COP15. Natural resources management addresses air and water quality preservation, particularly critical as the Arabian Gulf faces increased salinity and contamination pressures from regional industrial expansion.

The circular economy track focuses on municipal waste diversion targets and electronic waste recycling protocols. Dubai aims to reduce general waste to landfill by 75 percent by 2040, a target requiring coordination across construction, retail, hospitality and manufacturing sectors. E-waste recycling emerges as a distinct sector: the UAE generated approximately 145,000 tonnes of e-waste in 2025, with less than 10 percent currently collected for formal recycling. New partnerships between waste management operators and technology refurbishment companies are positioning the UAE as a regional e-waste processing hub.

Environmental artificial intelligence represents the conference's forward-looking component, with sessions exploring AI applications in air quality monitoring using IoT sensor networks, water consumption optimization for desalination plants, building energy management across emirate infrastructure, and climate modelling for regional weather pattern prediction. Government agencies and corporate technology officers are positioned to pilot integrated systems across emirate infrastructure by end-2026.

Food security programming covers the emirate's supply chain diversification away from vulnerable import-dependent systems, with focus on vertical farming adoption and regional agricultural partnerships. The conference runs until 8 September.

The conference programme features dedicated sessions on carbon accounting methodologies aligned with international standards (GHG Protocol, ISO 14064). Government environmental agencies are implementing emissions tracking systems and establishing baseline emissions inventories for industrial facilities and municipal activities. Manufacturers face increasing pressure to report scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions and implement reduction targets aligned with national commitments.

Water management receives particular focus given the Arabian Gulf region's extreme water scarcity. Desalination plants, which dominate Gulf water supply, consume significant energy and generate concentrated brine waste requiring environmental management. The conference explores advanced desalination technologies (reverse osmosis efficiency improvements, forward osmosis) and brine management solutions including mineral recovery and environmental discharge protocols. Wastewater treatment and recycling for industrial and irrigation applications are positioned as critical components of water security and environmental sustainability strategies.
